title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing's rollout facts, licensing, controls and administrator-created policy route are supported. The governance checklist names policy configuration without a corresponding controls row, and the medium risk rating overstates the documented opt-in default.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to apply library default sensitivity labels to existing SharePoint files.
claims.quote: Enables auto-labeling of existing SharePoint files to match the default sensitivity label configured on their document library.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes closing labeling gaps for data at rest without manual user labeling.
claims.quote: This helps organizations close labeling gaps for data at rest and ensure consistent, secure-by-default protection across SharePoint libraries—without relying on manual user labeling.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn documents an auto-labeling policy that applies each selected library's default label to eligible existing files.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy that applies the default sensitivity label from each selected SharePoint document library to eligible existing files at rest.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The documented existing-files capability requires administrator policy configuration, supporting admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy

claims.claim: The separate library-default setting labels new uploaded files that have no label or a lower-priority label, subject to its override rules.
claims.quote: any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied if they don't already have a sensitivity label, or they have a sensitivity label but with lower priority

claims.claim: The separate library-default setting also labels existing files when users edit them, subject to its override rules.
claims.quote: any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied

claims.claim: The separate library-default page still lists existing files at rest as a limitation.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to existing files at rest in SharePoint.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The library-default page says a library default overrides a lower-priority label unless it was manually applied.
claims.quote: Default sensitivity label for a document library: Location-based labeling, applicable only for SharePoint. Overrides a lower-priority label unless manually applied.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: An encryption label can restrict who can open a file.
claims.quote: When a document, email, or meeting invite is encrypted, access to the content is restricted, so that it: Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.

claims.claim: A sensitivity label can carry content-marking or encryption settings.
claims.quote: you might want lower sensitivity content (such as a "General" label) to have just a header or footer applied, while higher sensitivity content (such as a "Confidential" label) should have a watermark and encryption.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The user-defined permissions configuration described on the library-default page is unsuitable for a library default.
claims.quote: Let users assign permissions when they apply the label and the checkbox In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions is selected. This setting is sometimes referred to as "user-defined permissions".

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A label whose user access expires at a value other than Never is unsuitable for a library default.
claims.quote: some label configurations that apply encryption aren't suitable for SharePoint, and so don't support a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library: ... User access to content expires is set to a value other than Never.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A label with Double Key Encryption selected is unsuitable for a library default.
claims.quote: some label configurations that apply encryption aren't suitable for SharePoint, and so don't support a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library: ... Double Key Encryption is selected.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Site admin permissions are required to apply or change the library's default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Site admin permissions are needed to apply and change the sensitivity label in SharePoint.

claims.claim: A library with SharePoint Information Rights Management enabled cannot select a default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: If a library is enabled for IRM, you won't be able to select a default sensitivity label.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Applied sensitivity label file audit event records application of library default labels.
claims.quote: To specifically identify when the label was applied because of the library's default sensitivity label, use the audit log search tool and the Applied sensitivity label file auditing event from the Sensitivity label activities group.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The library-default documentation identifies ActionScourceDetails value 6 as the library-default source.
claims.quote: identify the value for ActionScourceDetails. ... A value of 6 is used for when the label was applied because of the default sensitivity label for the document library.

claims.claim: Documentation does not specifically confirm that the existing-files policy uses the same audit source value.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint library existing files ActionScourceDetails. Read library-default monitoring and the auto-labeling page's existing-files policy section; the former gives 6 for its library setting, but the latter does not specify that policy's audit source value.

claims.claim: The tooltip for a file labeled by a library default reads This file has been automatically labeled.
claims.quote: When the label has been applied by this features, the tooltip for the label name displays This file has been automatically labeled.

claims.claim: The same tooltip also appears for labels applied by auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: this tooltip isn't exclusive to the default sensitivity label for a document library. It also displays when sensitivity labels are applied by using auto-labeling policies

claims.claim: The same tooltip also appears for a user's default label from a sensitivity label policy.
claims.quote: It also displays when sensitivity labels are applied by using auto-labeling policies or as a result of a user's default label from sensitivity label policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn provides no government-cloud rollout window for this policy option beyond the roadmap target reported by the briefing.
claims.quote: Searched: Apply default sensitivity labels existing files GCC. Read the auto-labeling existing-files section and government availability search excerpts; neither states this option's GCC, GCC High or DoD rollout window.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labeling, supporting the per-user licensing model.
claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services

claims.claim: User licensing requirements depend on the sensitivity-labeling features used.
claims.quote: the licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use.

claims.claim: Administrators need a license to manage sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Admins also need a license to manage sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: The getting-started page directs readers to the Purview service description for feature-level licensing requirements.
claims.quote: For sensitivity labels, see the Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labeling section and related PDF download for feature-level licensing requirements.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The existing-files capability is service-side labeling for files at rest.
claims.quote: Use this configuration when: ... You want service-side labeling for files at rest, instead of relying on users to open or edit each file.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 and Office 365 E5/A5/G5 are among the plans including client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/GOV/FLW ... | Office 365 E5/A5/G5 ... Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling | Included | Included

claims.claim: The auto-labeling page says E3 and Business Premium do not include auto-labeling of files and emails and require an E5 / P2-tier add-on.
claims.quote: You have E3 or Business Premium. Auto-labeling of files and emails isn't included at this SKU. Sensitivity labels and manual labeling are — auto-labeling requires an E5 / P2-tier add-on.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No separate licensing entitlement specific to extending library defaults to existing files is published beyond the documented auto-labeling requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint library existing files default licensing. Read the auto-labeling licensing and existing-files sections, Purview sensitivity-labeling licensing matrix, and library-default requirements; none names a separate entitlement for this policy subtype.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No meter specific to applying library defaults to existing files is published.
claims.quote: Searched: default library existing files meter licensing. Read the auto-labeling licensing and existing-files sections and Purview service description's sensitivity-labeling matrix; none identifies a meter for this policy subtype.

claims.claim: The library-default page's Requirements section names no license.
claims.quote: Requirements: ... created and published ... enabled sensitivity labels ... added support for PDFs ... IRM ... Site admin permissions ... Files must contain content to be labeled.

claims.claim: Library-default labels must be published with the Files & other data assets scope.
claims.quote: You've created and published sensitivity labels that include the label scope of Files & other data assets and these labels are published to the users who will select a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: You've enabled sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Labeling PDFs requires PDF support to be enabled in SharePoint.
claims.quote: To support sensitivity labels for PDFs, you've added support for PDFs in SharePoint.

claims.claim: The existing-files policy requires permission to create and manage auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: You have permissions to create and manage auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: The existing-files policy requires read access to site and library metadata used to identify libraries with defaults.
claims.quote: You have permission to read the SharePoint site and document library metadata required to identify libraries with default sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: The library default label is reached through document library > Settings > Library settings > Default sensitivity labels in SharePoint.
claims.quote: In SharePoint, navigate to the document library > Settings > Library settings. ... From the Library settings flyout pane, select Default sensitivity labels, and then select a label from the drop-down box.

claims.claim: POST https://<site-url>/_api/web/lists(guid'<library-guid>') updates a library with X-HTTP-Method: MERGE.
claims.quote: The following example shows how to update a list by using the MERGE method. ... POST https://{site_url}/_api/web/lists(guid'{list_guid}') ... X-HTTP-Method: "MERGE"

claims.claim: DefaultSensitivityLabelForLibrary is the library REST setting for its default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: For the default library label, set the DefaultSensitivityLabelForLibrary parameter by using REST API on a library.

claims.claim: Extend protection on download, copy, or move is a different scenario and should not be selected for ordinary library defaults.
claims.quote: From the Library settings pane, select a sensitivity label and don't select the checkbox Extend protection on download, copy, or move. This setting is currently in preview and supports a different labeling scenario.

claims.claim: No administrator UI is documented for the tenant-level DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling switch.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling admin center UI; DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling admin center settings. Read library-default turn-off instructions and search results; these document PowerShell, not a tenant UI for this switch.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling $true disables the existing library-default feature tenant-wide.
claims.quote: This is a tenant-level setting that requires you to use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling parameter set to True ... Set-SpoTenant -DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling $true

claims.claim: The tenant-level switch takes about 15 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: As with all tenant-level configuration changes for SharePoint, it takes about 15 minutes for the change to take effect.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Documentation does not confirm whether the tenant library-default switch stops the separate existing-files auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Searched: DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling existing policy. Read library-default turn-off instructions, Set-SPOTenant search excerpt and existing-files policy instructions; none states how this switch affects that separate policy type.

claims.claim: Audit > Search in the Microsoft Purview portal reaches audit search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <date> -EndDate <date> -RecordType <ID> queries audit records without modifying them.
claims.quote: runs Search-UnifiedAuditLog to search for audit log entries within a specified date range and record type. ... Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate 2023/03/12 -EndDate 2023/03/20 -RecordType <ID>

claims.claim: Disabling library defaults retains the library's selection but deactivates it.
claims.quote: The label selection for the document library remains but is deactivated so new files won't have the selected sensitivity label applied.

claims.claim: Disabling library defaults does not remove labels already applied as defaults.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that were applied as a default label aren't removed.

claims.claim: Changes to the library-default setting can be audited through the Updated list event.
claims.quote: To audit the configuration setting for this feature, use the Updated list auditing event from the SharePoint list activities group.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to select specific SharePoint sites rather than All for the existing-files policy.
claims.quote: Select specific SharePoint sites rather than All.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to review simulation results before turning on the existing-files policy.
claims.quote: Review the simulation results before you turn on the policy to confirm that the expected SharePoint sites, document libraries, default library labels, and files are included.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist's instruction to configure and review the existing-files auto-labeling policy has no corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: Select specific SharePoint sites and review simulation results before turning on the auto-labeling policy. Table rows: library default label; tenant-level library-default switch; audit search.
claims.fix: The checklist step 'Select specific SharePoint sites and review simulation results before turning on the auto-labeling policy for existing files' has no corresponding row in the controls table. This is a coverage finding, not a request to add a row during correction.

claims.claim: The medium risk rating does not match the scale's low category for a change that does nothing until an administrator opts in.
claims.quote: risk: medium; defaultState: admin-opt-in. Rationale: Learn documents an administrator-created auto-labeling policy, reviewed in simulation before it is turned on.
claims.fix: Set risk to low and replace its rationale with: 'Low. Existing files are labelled only after an administrator creates and turns on an auto-labeling policy; review simulation results before enabling it.'
